(a) the term ‘‘entity’’ means a partnership, association, trust, joint venture, 
corporation, group, subgroup, or other organization; 
(b) the term ‘‘foreign financial institution’’ means any foreign entity that 
is engaged in the business of accepting deposits, making, granting, transfer-
ring, holding, or brokering loans or credits, or purchasing or selling foreign 
exchange, securities, commodity futures or options, or procuring purchasers 
and sellers thereof, as principal or agent. It includes, but is not limited 
to, depository institutions, banks, savings banks, money service businesses, 
trust companies, securities brokers and dealers, commodity futures and op-
tions brokers and dealers, forward contract and foreign exchange merchants, 
securities and commodities exchanges, clearing corporations, investment 
companies, employee benefit plans, dealers in precious metals, stones, or 
jewels, and holding companies, affiliates, or subsidiaries of any of the fore-
going. The term does not include the international financial institutions 
identified in 22 U.S.C. 262r(c)(2), the International Fund for Agricultural 
Development, the North American Development Bank, or any other inter-
national financial institution so notified by the Secretary of the Treasury; 
(c) the term ‘‘Government of Iran’’ includes the Government of Iran, any 
political subdivision, agency, or instrumentality thereof, including the Central 
Bank of Iran, and any person owned or controlled by, or acting for or 
on behalf of, the Government of Iran; 
(d) the term ‘‘Iran’’ means the Government of Iran and the territory of 
Iran and any other territory or marine area, including the exclusive economic 
zone and continental shelf, over which the Government of Iran claims sov-
ereignty, sovereign rights, or jurisdiction, provided that the Government 
of Iran exercises partial or total de facto control over the area or derives 
a benefit from economic activity in the area pursuant to international arrange-
ments; 
(e) the term ‘‘knowingly,’’ with respect to conduct, a circumstance, or 
a result, means that a person has actual knowledge, or should have known, 
of the conduct, the circumstance, or the result; 
(f) the term ‘‘person’’ means an individual or entity; and 
(g) the term ‘‘United States person’’ means any United States citizen, 
permanent resident alien, entity organized under the laws of the United 
States or any jurisdiction within the United States (including foreign 
branches), or any person in the United States. 
Sec. 9. For those persons whose property and interests in property are 
blocked pursuant to this order who might have a constitutional presence 
in the United States, I find that because of the ability to transfer funds 
or other assets instantaneously, prior notice to such persons of measures 
to be taken pursuant to this order would render those measures ineffectual. 
I therefore determine that for these measures to be effective in addressing 
the national emergency declared in Executive Order 12957, there need be 
no prior notice of a listing or determination made pursuant to section 
1 of this order. 
Sec. 10. The Secretary of the Treasury, in consultation with the Secretary 
of State, is hereby authorized to take such actions, including adopting rules 
and regulations, and to employ all powers granted to the President by 
IEEPA as may be necessary to implement this order. The Secretary of the 
Treasury may, consistent with applicable law, redelegate any of these func-
tions within the Department of the Treasury. All agencies shall take all 
appropriate measures within their authority to implement this order. 
Sec. 11. (a) Nothing in this order shall be construed to impair or otherwise 
affect: 
(i) the authority granted by law to an executive department or agency, 
or the head thereof; or 
(ii) the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget 
relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals.

(c) This order is not intended to, and does not, create any right or benefit,

Sec. 12. The measures taken pursuant to this order are in response to 
actions of the Government of Iran occurring after the conclusion of the

46589
Federal Register 
Vol. 54, No. 212
Presidential Documents
Friday, November 3, 1989
Title 3— Executive Order 12695
The President Delegation of Debt Relief Authority
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and laws of the 
United States of America, including the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961, as 
amended, and section 572 of the Foreign Operations, Export Financing, and 
Related Programs Appropriations Act, 1989 (Public Law 100-461, 102 Stab 
2268), and in order to delegate certain relief authority to the Administrator of 
the Agency for International Development, it is hereby ordered as follows:
Section 1 . Delegation o f Presidential Authority under Section 572 of the  
Foreign Operations, Export Financing, and Related Programs Appropriations 
Act, 1989. Section l-102(a) of Executive Order No. 12163, as amended, is 
further amended by (A) deleting “and” at the end of subsection (9), (B) 
deleting the period and inserting and” at the end of subsection (10), and (C) 
adding a subsection (11) as follows:
“(11) section 572 of the Foreign Operations, Export Financing, and Related 
Programs Appropriations Act, 1989 (Public Law 100-461), to be exercised by 
the Administrator of the Agency for International Development within IDCA, 
with the concurrence of the Development Coordination Committee, as estab­
lished by section 640B of the Act and as provided for herein.”.
Sec. 2. Effective Date. This order shall take effect immediately.
[FR Doc. 89-26182 
Filed 11-2-89; 11:12 am] 
Billing code 3195-Ol-M
THE WHITE HOUSE, ( y  
November 1, 1989.

THE PRESIDENT 10069
EXECUTIVE ORDER 11713
D elegating C ertain Functions Vested in the President to the  
Adm inistrator o f General Services
By virtue of the authority vested in me by section 301 of title 3 of 
the United States Code, and as President of the United States, it is 
hereby ordered as follows:
S e c t i o n 1. Section 1  of Executive Order No. 11609 of July 22, 1971, 
is hereby amended by adding at the end thereof the following new 
paragraphs:
“ (22) The authority of the President under section 372 of title 2 of 
the Canal Zone Code to approve transfers between departments and 
agencies of certain property in the Canal Zone.
“ (23) The authority of the President under section 62(d)  of title 2 
of the Canal Zone Code to approve the valuation of properties and other 
assets being transferred between the Panama Canal Company and other 
Government agencies.”
S e c. 2. All actions heretofore taken by the President, the Director of 
the Bureau of the Budget, or the Director of the Office of Management 
and Budget in respect of matters affected by the amendment made by 
section 1  of this order and in force at the time of the issuance of this 
order, including any regulations prescribed or approved by any of them 
in respect of such matters, shall, except as may be inconsistent with the 
provisions of this order, remain in effect until amended, modified, or 
revoked pursuant to the authority conferred by this order unless sooner 
terminated by operation of law.
Sec. 3. Executive Order No. 11541 of July 1, 1970, is superseded to 
the extent that it is inconsistent with this order.
T h e W h i t e H o u s e,
April 21, 1973.
[FR D oc.73-8054 Filed 4 -2 3 -7 3 ;1 0 :13 am]
FEDERAL REGISTER, VOL. 38, N O . 78— TUESDAY, APRIL 24, 1973

{"actor_id":"EO:12356","char_end":38153,"char_start":38042,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"unknown","effective_date":null,"effective_wording":[{"char_end":31244,"char_start":30842,"text":"The agency regulation or guideline shall remain in  \neffect pending a prompt decision on the appeal;\n(4) have the authority to conduct on-site reviews of the information security  \nprogram of each agency that generates or handles classified information and  \nto require of each agency those reports, information, and other cooperation  \nthat may be necessary to fulfill the Director’s responsibilities."},{"char_end":32458,"char_start":31559,"text":"The denial of access  \nshall remain in effect pending a prompt decision on the appeal;\n(5) review requests for original classification authority from agencies or offi­\ncials not granted original classification authority and, if deemed appropriate,  \nrecommend presidential approval;\n(6) /consider and take action on complaints and suggestions from persons  \nwithin or outside the Government with respect to the administration of the  \ninformation security program;\n(7) have the authority to prescribe, after consultation with affected agencies,  \nstandard forms that will promote the implementation of the information  \nsecurity program;\n(8) report at least annually to the President through the National Security  \nCouncil on the implementation of this Order, and\n(9) have the authority to convene and cliair interagency meetings to discuss  \nmatters pertaining to the information security program."},{"char_end":32843,"char_start":32511,"text":"Agencies that originate or handle classified information shall: %  -\n(a) designate a senior agency official to direct and administer its information  \nsecurity program, which shall include an active oversight and security educa­\ntion program to ensure effective implementation of this Order;\n(b) promulgate implementing regulations."},{"char_end":38153,"char_start":38042,"text":"(d) Executive Order No. 12065 of June 28,1978, as amended, is revoked as of  \nthe effective date of this Order."},{"char_end":38209,"char_start":38154,"text":"(e) This Order shall become effective on August 1,1982."}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:12163>EO:12356","names_target":false,"notes":"Machine lead only; no legal ending or revival asserted. maturity of the varities  \nof avocados covered by this amendment  \nwere made at the meeting of said com­\nmittee on August 14, 1956, after con­\nsideration of all available information  \nrelative {"actor_id":"EO:12107","char_end":6902,"char_start":6715,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"unknown","effective_date":null,"effective_wording":[{"char_end":1383,"char_start":1105,"text":"The establishment o f \nthe Office o f Personnel Management and o f the positions o f Director,* Deputy \nDirector, and Associate Directors o f that Office, as provided in Sections 101 \nand 103 o f Reorganization Plan No. 2 o f 1978, shall be effective on January 1, \n1979.\n1-102."},{"char_end":1598,"char_start":1420,"text":"Section 102 o f Reorganization Plan No. 2 o f \n1978, transferring functions to the Director o f the Office o f Personnel Man­\nagement, shall be effective on January i, 1979.\n1-2."},{"char_end":1959,"char_start":1704,"text":"The redesignation o f the \nCivil Service Commission as the .Merit Systems Protection Board and o f the \nCommissioners as Members o f the Board as provided in Section 201 o f \nReorganization Plan No. 2 o f 1978 shall be effective on January 1, 1979.\n1-202."},{"char_end":2237,"char_start":2029,"text":"The functions o f the \nMerit Systems Protection Board as provided in Section 202 and the savings \nprovisions o f Section 203 o f Reorganization Plan No. 2 o f 1978 shall be \neffective on January 1, 1979.\n1-3."},{"char_end":2543,"char_start":2335,"text":"The establishment o f the \nOffice o f Special Counsel to the Merit Systems Protection Board as provided \nin Section 204(a) o f Reorganization Plan No. 2 o f 1978 shall be effective on \nJanuary 1, 1979.\n1-302."},{"char_end":2800,"char_start":2591,"text":"The transfer o f functions provided \nfor in Section 204(b) and the performance o f functions set forth in Section \n204(c)-(g) o f Reorganization Plan No. 2 o f 1978 shall be effective on January \n1, 1979.\n1-4."},{"char_end":3251,"char_start":3000,"text":"The establishment o f the Federal Labor Relations Authority \nas provided in Section 301 and o f the Office o f General Counsel o f the \nAuthority as provided in Section 302 o f Reorganization Plan No. 2 o f 1978 \nshall be effective on January 1, 1979."},{"char_end":3724,"char_start":3414,"text":"The continuation o f the Federal \nService Impasses Panel established under Executive Order No. 11491, as \namended, as a distinct organizational entity within the Federal Labor Relations \nAuthority as provided in Section 303 o f Reorganization Plan No. 2 o f 1978, \nshall be effective on January 1, 1979.\n1-403."},{"char_end":4018,"char_start":3725,"text":"F u n ctio n s  o f  the F ed era l L a b o r R e la tio n s  A u th o rity , the G en era l Counsel, \na n d  the F ed era l S ervice Impasses P a n e l The transfer o f functions provided for in \nSection 304 o f Reorganization Plan No. 2 o f 1978‘ shall be effective on January \n1, 1979.\n1-5."},{"char_end":4169,"char_start":4070,"text":"All other provisions o f Reorganization Plan \nNo. 2 o f 1978 shall be effective on January 1, 1979."},{"char_end":9501,"char_start":9217,"text":"The Director may secure effective \nimplementation o f the civil service laws, rules, and regulations, and all Execu­\ntive orders imposing responsibilities on the Office by:\n(a) Investigating the qualifications and suitability o f applicants for posi­\ntions in the competitive service."},{"char_end":14927,"char_start":14815,"text":"The amendments to rules shall be \neffective on January 1, 1979, to the extent provided by law on that date.\n2-2."},{"char_end":15997,"char_start":15716,"text":"Any rules, regulations, directives, instructions or \nother actions taken pursuant to the authority delegated to the Director o f the \nOffice o f Personnel Management shall remain in effect until amended, modi­\nfied, or revoked pursuant to the delegations made by this Order.\n2-202."},{"char_end":16431,"char_start":16026,"text":"All personnel actions and decisions affecting em­\nployees or applicants for employment made on or before January 11, 1979 \nshall continue to be governed by the applicable Executive order, and the rules \nand regulations implementing that Order, to the same extent as if that Execu­\ntive order had not been revoked effective January 11, 1979 unless amended, \nmodified or revoked pursuant to this Order.\n2-3."},{"char_end":25809,"char_start":25461,"text":"Except as required by the Civil Service \nReform Act o f 1978 as its provisions become effective, in accord with Section \n7135 o f Title 5, United States Code, as amended, and in accord with Section \n902(a) o f that Act, the provisions o f this Order shall continue in effect, \naccording to its terms, until modified, terminated or suspended.\n2-403."},{"char_end":26849,"char_start":26742,"text":"Except as otherwise specifically provided in this \nOrder, this Order shall be effective on January 1, 1979."}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:10577>EO:12107","names_target":true,"notes":"Machine - **ACT:EO:10577>EO:12107@6bb1ea5f80de7f1c**; S7b054cd6ef591c3c4b920834; {"actor_id":"EO:12107","char_end":5684,"char_start":5513,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"unknown","effective_date":null,"effective_wording":[{"char_end":810,"char_start":551,"text":"The establishment of the Office of Personnel Management and of the positions of Director, Deputy Director, and Associate Directors of that Office, as provided in Sections 101 and 103 of Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1978, shall be effective on January 1, 1979."},{"char_end":1009,"char_start":842,"text":"Section 1-02 of Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1978, transferring functions to the Director of the Office of Personnel Management, shall be effective on January 1, 1979."},{"char_end":1338,"char_start":1099,"text":"The redesignation of the Civil Service Commission as the Merit Systems Protection Board and of the Commissioners as Members of the Board as provided in Section 201 of Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1978 shall be effective on January 1, 1979."},{"char_end":1592,"char_start":1396,"text":"The functions of the Merit Systems Protection Board as provided in Section 202 and the savings provisions of Section 203 of Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1978 shall be effective on January 1, 1979."},{"char_end":1869,"char_start":1675,"text":"The establishment of the Office of Special Counsel to the Merit Systems Protection Board as provided in Section 204(a) of Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1978 shall be effective on January 1, 1979."},{"char_end":2109,"char_start":1912,"text":"The transfer of functions provided for in Section 204(b) and the performance of functions set forth in Section 204(c)-(g) of Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1978 shall be effective on January 1, 1979."},{"char_end":2499,"char_start":2257,"text":"The establishment of the Federal Labor Relations Authority as provided in Section 301 and of the Office of General Counsel of the Authority as provided in Section 302 of Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1978 shall be effective on January 1, 1979."},{"char_end":2840,"char_start":2544,"text":"The continuation of the Federal Service Impasses Panel established under Executive Order No. 11491, as amended, as a distinct organizational entity within the Federal Labor Relations Authority as provided in Section 303 of Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1978, shall be effective on January 1, 1979."},{"char_end":3091,"char_start":2962,"text":"The transfer of functions provided for in Section 304 of Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1978 shall be effective on January 1, 1979."},{"char_end":3138,"char_start":3115,"text":"General Effective Date."},{"char_end":3235,"char_start":3139,"text":"All other provisions of Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1978 shall be effective on January 1, 1979."},{"char_end":7984,"char_start":7816,"text":"The Director may secure effective implementation of the civil service laws, rules, and regulations, and all Executive orders imposing responsibilities on the Office by:"},{"char_end":13282,"char_start":13176,"text":"The amendments to rules shall be effective on January 1, 1979, to the extent provided by law on that date."},{"char_end":14262,"char_start":13994,"text":"Any rules, regulations, directives, instructions or other actions taken pursuant to the authority delegated to the Director of the Office of Personnel Management shall remain in effect until amended, modified, or revoked pursuant to the delegations made by this Order."},{"char_end":14684,"char_start":14290,"text":"All personnel actions and decisions affecting employees or applicants for employment made on or before January 11, 1979, shall continue to be governed by the applicable Executive order, and the rules and regulations implementing that Order, to the same extent as if that Executive order had not been revoked effective January 11, 1979 unless amended, modified or revoked pursuant to this Order."},{"char_end":23393,"char_start":23059,"text":"Except as required by the Civil Service Reform Act of 1978 as its provisions become effective, in accord with Section 7135 of Title 5, United States Code, as amended, and in accord with Section 902 (a) of that Act, the provisions of this Order shall continue in effect, according to its terms, until modified, terminated or suspended."},{"char_end":24190,"char_start":24175,"text":"Effective Date."},{"char_end":24297,"char_start":24191,"text":"Except as otherwise specifically provided in this Order, this Order shall be effective on January 1, 1979."}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:10577>EO:12107@6bb1ea5f80de7f1c","names_target":true,"notes":"Machine lead only; no legal ending or revival asserted. Effective wording is ambiguous, section-specific, or has no determinable date.","provision_label":"SECTION 2","reaches_target_via":"","savings_phrases":["The functions of the Merit Systems Protection Board as provided in Section 202 and the savings provisions of Section 203 of Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1978 shall be effective on January 1, 1979.","Savings Provision.","Except as required by the Civil Service Reform Act of 1978 as its provisions become effective, in accord with Section 7135 of Title 5, United States Code, as amended, and in accord with Section 902 (a) of that Act, the provisions of this Order shall continue in effect, according to its terms, until modified, terminated or suspended."],"scope":"partial","signing_date":"1978-12-28","target_id":"EO:10577","verb":"amend"}

- **ACT:EO:10577>EO:13467**; S023de79d8eb490afcb428b20; {"actor_id":"EO:13467","char_end":17853,"char_start":17312,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"unknown","effective_date":null,"effective_wording":[{"char_end":1951,"char_start":1347,"text":"Executive branch policies and procedures relating to \nsuitability, contractor employee fitness, eligibility to hold a sensitive position, \naccess to federally controlled facilities and information systems, and eligi-\nbility for access to classified information shall be aligned using consistent \nstandards to the extent possible, provide for reciprocal recognition, and \nshall ensure cost-effective, timely,and efficient protection of the national \ninterest, while providing fair treatment to those upon whom the Federal \nGovernment relies to conduct our Nation’s business and protect national \nsecurity."},{"char_end":8369,"char_start":7558,"text":"(b) The aligned system shall employ updated and consistent standards and \nmethods, enable innovations with enterprise information technology capabili-\nties and end-to-end automation to the extent practicable, and ensure that \nrelevant information maintained by agencies can be accessed and shared \nVerDate Aug<31>2005 18:32 Jul 01, 2008 Jkt 214001 PO 00000 Frm 00004 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\02JYE0.SGM 02JYE0hsrobinson on PROD1PC76 with PROPOSALS2\n=== PDF page 3 of 6 ===\n38105 Federal Register / Vol. 73, No. 128 / Wednesday, July 2, 2008 / Presidential Documents \nrapidly across the executive branch, while protecting national security, pro-\ntecting privacy-related information, ensuring resulting decisions are in the \nnational interest, and providing the Federal Government with an effective \nworkforce."},{"char_end":11953,"char_start":11412,"text":"(e) The Chair may, to ensure the effective implementation of the policy \nset forth in section 1.1 of this order and to the extent consistent with \nlaw, assign, in whole or in part, to the head of any agency (solely or \njointly) any function within the Council ’s responsibility relating to alignment \nand improvement of investigations and determinations of suitability, con-\ntractor employee fitness, eligibility for logical and physical access, eligibility \nfor access to classified information, or eligibility to hold a sensitive position."},{"char_end":12890,"char_start":12501,"text":"As the Suitability Executive Agent, the Director \nof the Office of Personnel Management will continue to be responsible \nfor developing and implementing uniform and consistent policies and proce-\ndures to ensure the effective, efficient, and timely completion of investiga-\ntions and adjudications relating to determinations of suitability and eligibility \nfor logical and physical access."},{"char_end":15137,"char_start":12980,"text":"The Security Executive Agent: \n(i) shall direct the oversight of investigations and determinations of eligi-\nbility for access to classified information or eligibility to hold a sensitive \nposition made by any agency; \n(ii) shall be responsible for developing uniform and consistent policies \nand procedures to ensure the effective, efficient, and timely completion \nof investigations and adjudications relating to determinations of eligibility \nfor access to classified information or eligibility to hold a sensitive position; \n(iii) may issue guidelines and instructions to the heads of agencies to \nensure appropriate uniformity, centralization, efficiency, effectiveness, and \ntimeliness in processes relating to determinations by agencies of eligibility \nfor access to classified information or eligibility to hold a sensitive position; \n(iv) shall serve as the final authority to designate an agency or agencies \nto conduct investigations of persons who are proposed for access to classi-\nfied information to ascertain whether such persons satisfy the criteria \nfor obtaining and retaining access to classified information or eligibility \nto hold a sensitive position; \n(v) shall serve as the final authority to designate an agency or agencies \nto determine eligibility for access to classified information in accordance \nwith Executive Order 12968 of August 2, 1995; \n(vi) shall ensure reciprocal recognition of eligibility for access to classified \ninformation among the agencies, including acting as the final authority \nto arbitrate and resolve disputes among the agencies involving the reci-\nprocity of investigations and determinations of eligibility for access to \nclassified information or eligibility to hold a sensitive position; and \n(vii) may assign, in whole or in part, to the head of any agency (solely \nor jointly) any of the functions detailed in (i) through (vi), above, with \nthe agency ’s exercise of such assigned functions to be subject to the \nSecurity Executive Agent ’s oversight and with such terms and conditions \n(including approval by the Security Executive Agent) as the Security Execu-\ntive Agent determines appropriate."},{"char_end":20366,"char_start":19744,"text":"VerDate Aug<31>2005 18:32 Jul 01, 2008 Jkt 214001 PO 00000 Frm 00007 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\02JYE0.SGM 02JYE0hsrobinson on PROD1PC76 with PROPOSALS2\n=== PDF page 6 of 6 ===\n38108 Federal Register / Vol. 73, No. 128 / Wednesday, July 2, 2008 / Presidential Documents \n(g) Existing delegations of authority made pursuant to Executive Order 13381 \nof June 27, 2005, as amended, to any agency relating to granting eligibility \nfor access to classified information and conducting investigations shall 13 \nremain in effect, subject to the exercise of authorities pursuant to this \norder to revise or revoke such delegation."}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:10577>EO:13467","names_target":true,"notes":"Machine lead only; no legal ending or revival asserted. Government’s personnel, property, and information."},{"char_end":13478,"char_start":12783,"text":"To help fulfill these responsibilities, there shall be a primary executive \nbranch investigative sustained \nby an enhanced risk-management approach that facilitates early detection \nof issues by an informed, aware, and responsible Federal workforce; results \nin quality decisions enabled by improved vetting capabilities; and advances \nGovernment-wide capabilities through enterprise approaches. \n‘‘(d) The appointment or retention of each covered individual shall be \nsubject to an 1.3(l) are added to Executive Order 13467 \nto read as follows: \n‘‘(k) ‘Fitness’ means the level of character and conduct determined nec-\nessary for an individual to perform work for or on behalf of defined in Executive Order 13488 \nof January 16, 2009, as amended. \n‘‘(l) ‘Investigation’ means the collection and analysis of pertinent facts \nand data to support a determination of whether a covered individual \nis, and continues to be: \n‘‘(i) eligible for access to classified information; \n‘‘(ii) eligible to hold a sensitive position; \n‘‘(iii) suitable or fit for Federal employment; \n‘‘(iv) fit to perform work for or on behalf of the Federal Government \nas a contractor or nonappropriated fund employee; or \n‘‘(v) authorized to be issued a Federal credential.’’ \n(k) secure personnel background investigations pursuant to law, \nrule, regulation, or Executive Order.’’ \n(l) Redesignated section 1.3(o) of Executive Order 13467 is revised to \nread as follows: \n‘‘(o) ‘Sensitive Position’ means any position within or in support of a \ndepartment or agency, the occupant of which could bring about, by virtue \nof the nature of the position, a material adverse protecting civil rights and civil liberties, ensuring resulting deci-\nsions are in the national interest and in accordance with due process \nrequirements, and providing the Federal Government with credential; \n‘‘(iii) shall develop guidelines on reporting and recording determinations \nof eligibility for a PIV credential; \n‘‘(iv) shall develop standards for unfavorable determinations of eligibility \nfor a PIV credential, including procedures for denying and revoking the \neligibility for a PIV credential, for reconsideration of unfavorable deter-\nminations, and for rendering the PIV credential inoperable; \n‘‘(v) shall develop standards and procedures for suspending eligibility \nfor a PIV credential when there is a reasonable basis to believe there \nmay be an unacceptable risk pending an inquiry or investigation, including \nspecial standards and procedures for imminent risk; \n‘‘(vi) shall be responsible for developing uniform and consistent policies \nand procedures to ensure the effective, efficient, timely, and secure comple-\ntion of investigations and adjudications relating to eligibility for a PIV \ncredential; \n‘‘(vii) may develop guidelines and back-\nground investigation and adjudication programs to determine whether they \nare being implemented according to this order; \n‘‘(iii) shall be responsible for developing and issuing uniform and con-\nsistent policies and procedures to ensure the effective, efficient, timely, \nand secure completion of investigations, polygraphs, and adjudications \nrelating to determinations of eligibility for access to classified information \nor eligibility to hold a sensitive position; \n‘‘(iv) may issue guidelines and instructions to the heads of agencies \nto ensure appropriate uniformity, centralization, efficiency, effectiveness, \ntimeliness, and security in processes relating to determinations by agencies \nof eligibility for access to classified information or eligibility to hold \na sensitive position, to include such matters as investigations, polygraphs, \nadjudications, and reciprocity; \n‘‘(v) may, if consistent with the national security, authorize exceptions \nto or waivers of national security investigative requirements, and may \nissue implementing or clarifying guidance as necessary; \n‘‘(vi) shall serve as the final authority to designate an agency or agencies, \nto the extent that it is not practicable to use the National Background \nInvestigations Bureau, to conduct investigations of persons who are pro-\nposed for access to classified information or for eligibility to hold a sen-\nsitive position to ascertain whether such persons satisfy the criteria for \nobtaining and retaining access to classified information or eligibility to \nhold a sensitive position; \n‘‘(vii) shall serve as the final authority to designate an agency or agencies \nto determine eligibility for access to classified information or eligibility \nto hold a sensitive position in accordance with Executive Order 12968 \nof August 2, 1995, as amended; \n‘‘(viii) shall ensure reciprocal recognition of eligibility for access to \nclassified information or eligibility to hold a sensitive position among \nthe agencies, including acting as the final authority to arbitrate and resolve \ndisputes among the agencies involving the reciprocity of investigations \nand adjudications of eligibility; and \n‘‘(ix) may assign, in whole or in part, to the head of any agency (solely \nor jointly) any of the functions detailed in (i) through (viii) of this sub-\nsection, with the agency’s exercise of such assigned functions to be subject \nto the Security Executive Agent’s oversight and with such terms and \nconditions (including approval by the Security Executive Agent) as the \nSecurity Executive Agent determines appropriate. \n‘‘(f) Nothing in this section shall be construed in a manner that would \nlimit the authorities of the Director of the Office of Personnel Management, \nthe Director of National Intelligence, or the Secretary of Defense under \nlaw.’’ \n(t) Redesignated section 2.6 of Executive Order 13467 is revised to read \nas 13488 of January 16, 2009, as amended; and authorization \nto be issued a Federal credential for logical and physical access to federally \ncontrolled facilities or information systems; \n‘‘(2) provide effective, efficient, and secure personnel background inves-\ntigations for the Federal Government; \n‘‘(3) provide the Council information, to the extent permitted by law, \non matters of performance, timeliness, capacity, information technology \nmodernization, continuous performance improvement, and other relevant \naspects of NBIB operations; \n‘‘(4) be headquartered in or near Washington, District of Columbia; \n‘‘(5) have dedicated resources, including but not limited to a senior \nprivacy and civil liberties official; \n‘‘(6) institutionalize interagency collaboration and leverage expertise \nacross the executive branch; \n‘‘(7) continuously improve investigative operations, emphasizing infor-\nmation accuracy and protection, and regularly integrate best practices, \nincluding those identified by subject matter experts from industry, aca-\ndemia, or other relevant sources; \n‘‘(8) conduct personnel background investigations in accordance with \nuniform and consistent policies, procedures, standards, and requirements \nestablished by the Security Executive Agent and the Suitability and \nCredentialing Executive Agent exercising its Suitability Executive Agent \nfunctions; and \n‘‘(9) conduct other personnel background investigations as authorized \nby law, rule, regulation, or Executive Order.’’ \n‘‘(b) The Secretary of Defense shall design, develop, deploy, operate, secure, \ndefend, and continuously update and modernize, as necessary, vetting \ninformation technology systems that support all background investigation \nprocesses conducted by the chronology does not decide legal effect.","provision_text":"(v) Section 3 of Executive Order 13467 is revised to read as follows:\n\n\"Sec. 3. General Provisions. (a) Executive Order 13381 of June 27, 2005, as amended, and Executive Order 10450 of April 27, 1953, as amended, are revoked. By revoking Executive Order 10450 of April 27, 1953, as amended, there is no intent to alter the requirement for an investigation for national security purposes or the \"clearly consistent with the interest of national security\" standard prescribed by that Executive Order for making the determinations referenced in section 2.7(b)(ii). Further, suitability, fitness, credentialing, and national security eligibility regulations, standards and guidance issued by, or interagency agreements entered into by, the Council, the Executive Agents, or any agency pursuant to Executive Order 10450 of\n\nApril 27, 1953, as amended, shall remain valid until superseded. Nothing in this order shall:\n\n\"(i) supersede, impede, or otherwise affect:\n\n\"(A) Executive Order 10577 of November 23, 1954, as amended;\n\n\"(B) Executive Order 12333 of December 4, 1981, as amended;\n\n\"(C) Executive Order 12829 of January 6, 1993, as amended; or\n\n\"(D) Executive Order 13526 of December 29, 2009; or\n\n\"(ii) diminish or otherwise affect the denial and revocation procedures provided to individuals covered by Executive Order 10865 of February 20, 1960, as amended; or\n\n\"(iii) be applied in such a way as to affect any administrative proceeding pending on the date of this order.\n\n\"(b) Executive Order 12968 of August 2, 1995, is amended:\n\n\"(i) by inserting: 'Sec. 3.5. Continuous Evaluation. An individual who has been determined to be eligible for or who currently has access to classified information shall be subject to continuous evaluation as further defined by and under standards (including, but not limited to, the frequency of such evaluation) as determined by the Director of National Intelligence.'; and\n\n\"(ii) by striking 'the Security Policy Board shall make recommendations to the President through the Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs' in section 6.3(a) and inserting in lieu thereof 'the Director of National Intelligence shall serve as the final authority';\n\n\"(iii) by striking 'Security Policy Board' and inserting in lieu thereof 'Security Executive Agent' in each instance;\n\n\"(iv) by striking 'the Board' in section 1.1(j) and inserting in lieu thereof 'the Security Executive Agent'; and\n\n\"(v) by inserting 'or appropriate automated procedures' in section 3.1(b) after 'by appropriately trained adjudicative personnel'.\n\n\"(c) Provisions of Executive Order 12968 of August 2, 1995, as amended, that apply to eligibility for access to classified information shall apply to eligibility to hold any sensitive position regardless of whether that sensitive position requires access to classified information, subject to the Security Executive Agent issuing implementing or clarifying guidance regarding requirements for sensitive positions. Nothing in this order shall supersede, impede, or otherwise affect the remainder of Executive Order 12968 of August 2, 1995, as amended.\n\n\"(d) Nothing in this order shall be construed to impair or otherwise affect the:\n\n\"(i) authority granted by law to a department or agency, or the head thereof; or\n\n\"(ii) functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals.\n\n\"(e) This order shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and subject to the availability of appropriations.\n\n\"(f) Existing delegations of authority made pursuant to Executive Order 13381 of June 27, 2005, as amended, to any agency relating to granting eligibility for access to classified information shall remain in effect, subject to the exercise of authorities pursuant to this order to revise or revoke such delegation.\n\n\"(g) Existing delegations of authority made by the Office of Personnel Management to any agency relating to suitability or fitness shall remain in effect, subject to the exercise of authorities to revise or revoke such delegations.\n\n\"(h) If any provision of this order or the application of such provision is held to be invalid, the remainder of this order shall not be affected.\n\n\"(i) This order is not intended to, and does not, create any right or benefit, substantive or procedural, enforceable at law or in equity by any party against the United States, its departments, agencies, or entities, its officers, employees, or agents, or any other person.\"","sections_touched":["Section 3","section 2","section 6","section 1","section 3"],"signing_date":"2017-01-17","source":{"acceptable_as_original":false,"archival_id":"app:node/218590","filing_date":null,"grade":"mirror_transcription","instrument_id":"EO:13764","location_confidence":"medium","location_verified":false,"page_or_item":"Executive Order 13764—Amending the Civil Service Rules, Executive Order 13488, and Executive Order 13467 To Modernize the Executive Branch-Wide Governance Structure and Processes for Security Clearances, Suitability and Fitness for Employment, and Credentialing, and Related Matters; - **ACT:EO:12107>EO:12564**; S2dbc579cbbece9fc10f99a59; {"actor_id":"EO:12564","char_end":25394,"char_start":16273,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"agency_variable","effective_date":null,"effective_wording":[{"char_end":11647,"char_start":11023,"text":"L. 102–368, title XI, § 901, Sept. 23, 1992, 106 Stat. 1156, effective through Sept. 30, 1993, authorized Federal agencies to accept gifts of property, money, or anything else of value from non-Federal sources for extraordinary and unanticipated expenses incurred by agency employees in their personal capacity within areas designated as disaster areas pursuant to President’s declaration of a disaster resulting from Hurricane Andrew, Typhoon Omar, and Hurricane Iniki, directed agencies to establish written procedures to implement this program, and authorized agencies to accept gifts designated for individual employees."},{"char_end":15837,"char_start":11806,"text":"L. 102–54, § 13(b)(6), June 13, 1991, 105 Stat. 274, provided:\n“(a)\n(1)\n Except as provided in subsection (b) or (c), none of the funds appropriated or made available by this Act, or any other Act, with respect to any fiscal year, shall be available to administer or implement any drug testing pursuant to Executive Order Numbered 12564 (dated September 15, 1986) [set out as a note below], or any subsequent order, unless and until—\n“(A)\n the Secretary of Health and Human Services certifies in writing to the Committees on Appropriations of the House of Representatives and the Senate, and other appropriate committees of the Congress, that—\n“(i)\n each agency has developed a plan for achieving a drug-free workplace in accordance with Executive Order Numbered 12564 and applicable provisions of law (including applicable provisions of this section);\n“(ii)\n the Department of Health and Human Services, in addition to the scientific and technical guidelines dated February 13, 1987, and any subsequent amendments thereto, has, in accordance with paragraph (3), published mandatory guidelines which—\n“(I)\n establish comprehensive standards for all aspects of laboratory drug testing and laboratory procedures to be applied in carrying out Executive Order Numbered 12564, including standards which require the use of the best available technology for ensuring the full reliability and accuracy of drug tests and strict procedures governing the chain of custody of specimens collected for drug testing;\n“(II)\n specify the drugs for which Federal employees may be tested; and\n“(III)\n establish appropriate standards and procedures for periodic review of laboratories and criteria for certification and revocation of certification of laboratories to perform drug testing in carrying out Executive Order Numbered 12564; and\n“(iii)\n all agency drug-testing programs and plans established pursuant to Executive Order Numbered 12564 comply with applicable provisions of law, including applicable provisions of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 (29 U.S.C. 701 et seq.), title 5 of the United States Code, and the mandatory guidelines under clause (ii);\n“(B)\n the Secretary of Health and Human Services has submitted to the Congress, in writing, a detailed, agency-by-agency analysis relating to—\n“(i)\n the criteria and procedures to be applied in designating employees or positions for drug testing, including the justification for such criteria and procedures;\n“(ii)\n the position titles designated for random drug testing; and\n“(iii)\n the nature, frequency, and type of drug testing proposed to be instituted; and\n“(C)\n the Director of the Office of Management and Budget has submitted in writing to the Committees on Appropriations of the House of Representatives and the Senate a detailed, agency-by-agency analysis (as of the time of certification under subparagraph (A)) of the anticipated annual costs associated with carrying out Executive Order Numbered 12564 and all other requirements under this section during the 5-year period beginning on the date of the enactment of this Act [July 11, 1987].\n“(2)\n Notwithstanding subsection (g), for purposes of this subsection, the term “agency” means—\n“(A)\n the Executive Office of the President;\n“(B)\n an Executive department under section 101 of title 5, United States Code;\n“(C)\n the Environmental Protection Agency;\n“(D)\n the General Services Administration;\n“(E)\n the National Aeronautics and Space Administration;\n“(F)\n the Office of Personnel Management;\n“(G)\n the Small Business Administration;\n“(H)\n the United States Information Agency; and\n“(I)\n the Department of Veterans Affairs;\nexcept that such term does not include the Department of Transportation or any other entity (or component thereof) covered by subsection (b).\n“(3)\n Notwithstanding any provision of chapter 5 of title 5, United States Code, the mandatory guidelines to be published pursuant to subsection (a)(1)(A)(ii) shall be published and made effective exclusively according to the provisions of this paragraph."},{"char_end":19804,"char_start":16097,"text":"Following review and consideration of written comments, final mandatory guidelines shall be published in the Federal Register and shall become effective upon publication.\n“(b)\n(1)\n Nothing in subsection (a) shall limit or otherwise affect the availability of funds for drug testing by—\n“(A)\n the Department of Transportation;\n“(B)\n Department of Energy, for employees specifically involved in the handling of nuclear weapons or nuclear materials;\n“(C)\n any agency with an agency-wide drug-testing program in existence as of September 15, 1986; or\n“(D)\n any component of an agency if such component had a drug-testing program in existence as of September 15, 1986.\n“(2)\n The Departments of Transportation and Energy and any agency or component thereof with a drug-testing program in existence as of September 15, 1986—\n“(A)\n shall be brought into full compliance with Executive Order Numbered 12564 [set out as a note below] no later than the end of the 6-month period beginning on the date of the enactment of this Act [July 11, 1987]; and\n“(B)\n shall take such actions as may be necessary to ensure that their respective drug-testing programs or plans are brought into full compliance with the mandatory guidelines published under subsection (a)(1)(A)(ii) no later than 90 days after such mandatory guidelines take effect, except that any judicial challenge that affects such guidelines should not affect drug-testing programs or plans subject to this paragraph.\n“(c)\n In the case of an agency (or component thereof) other than an agency as defined by subsection (a)(2) or an agency (or component thereof) covered by subsection (b), none of the funds appropriated or made available by this Act, or any other Act, with respect to any fiscal year, shall be available to administer or implement any drug testing pursuant to Executive Order Numbered 12564 [set out as a note below], or any subsequent order, unless and until—\n“(1)\n the Secretary of Health and Human Services provides written certification with respect to that agency (or component) in accordance with clauses (i) and (iii) of subsection (a)(1)(A);\n“(2)\n the Secretary of Health and Human Services has submitted a written, detailed analysis with respect to that agency (or component) in accordance with subsection (a)(1)(B); and\n“(3)\n the Director of the Office of Management and Budget has submitted a written, detailed analysis with respect to that agency (or component) in accordance with subsection (a)(1)(C).\n“(d)\n Any Federal employee who is the subject of a drug test under any program or plan shall, upon written request, have access to—\n“(1)\n any records relating to such employee’s drug test; and\n“(2)\n any records relating to the results of any relevant certification, review, or revocation-of-certification proceedings, as referred to in subsection (a)(1)(A)(ii)(III).\n“(e)\n The results of a drug test of a Federal employee may not be disclosed without the prior written consent of such employee, unless the disclosure would be—\n“(1)\n to the employee’s medical review official (as defined in the scientific and technical guidelines referred to in subsection (a)(1)(A)(ii));\n“(2)\n to the administrator of any Employee Assistance Program in which the employee is receiving counseling or treatment or is otherwise participating;\n“(3)\n to any supervisory or management official within the employee’s agency having authority to take the adverse personnel action against such employee; or\n“(4)\n pursuant to the order of a court of competent jurisdiction where required by the United States Government to defend against any challenge against any adverse personnel action.\n“(f)\n [Terminated, effective May 15, 2000, see section 3003 of Pub."},{"char_end":20523,"char_start":19805,"text":"L. 104–66, as amended, set out as a note under section 1113 of Title 31, Money and Finance, and page 151 of House Document No. 103–7.]\n“(g)\n For purposes of this section, the terms ‘agency’ and ‘Employee Assistance Program’ each has the meaning given such term under section 7(b) of Executive Order Numbered 12564 [set out as a note below], as in effect on September 15, 1986.”\n[For abolition of United States Information Agency (other than Broadcasting Board of Governors and International Broadcasting Bureau), transfer of functions, and treatment of references thereto, see sections 6531, 6532, and 6551 of Title 22, Foreign Relations and Intercourse.]\nLimitation on Gratuities at Naval Shipbuilding Ceremonies\nPub."},{"char_end":24775,"char_start":24008,"text":"The use of illegal drugs, on or off duty, by Federal employees also can pose a serious health and safety threat to members of the public and to other Federal employees;\nThe use of illegal drugs, on or off duty, by Federal employees in certain positions evidences less than the complete reliability, stability, and good judgment that is consistent with access to sensitive information and creates the possibility of coercion, influence, and irresponsible action under pressure that may pose a serious risk to national security, the public safety, and the effective enforcement of the law; and\nFederal employees who use illegal drugs must themselves be primarily responsible for changing their behavior and, if necessary, begin the process of rehabilitating themselves."},{"char_end":36703,"char_start":36688,"text":"Effective Date."},{"char_end":36740,"char_start":36704,"text":"This Order is effective immediately."},{"char_end":47183,"char_start":46630,"text":"(a) All actions already taken by the President or by his delegates concerning matters affected by this order and in force when this order is issued, including any regulations issued under Executive Order 11222, Executive Order 12565, or statutory authority, shall, except as they are irreconcilable with the provisions of this order or terminate by operation of law or by Presidential action, remain in effect until properly amended, modified, or revoked pursuant to the authority conferred by this order or any regulations promulgated under this order."},{"char_end":53585,"char_start":53406,"text":"Nothing herein shall be construed to replace any agency policy currently in effect, if such policy is legally established, in writing, and consistent with the terms of this order."},{"char_end":59694,"char_start":59242,"text":"No. 13764, § 2, Jan. 17, 2017, 82 F.R. 8116, provided:\nBy the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the laws of the United States of America, including sections 1104(a)(1), 3301, and 7301 of title 5, United States Code, and in order to simplify and streamline the system of Federal Government personnel investigative and adjudicative processes to make them more efficient and effective, it is hereby ordered as follows:\nSection 1."},{"char_end":65950,"char_start":65917,"text":"Effective Date and Applicability."},{"char_end":66157,"char_start":65951,"text":"This order is effective upon issuance and is applicable to individuals newly appointed to excepted service positions or hired as contractor employees beginning 90 days from the effective date of this order."},{"char_end":74979,"char_start":74857,"text":"The delegation described in subsection (a) of this section shall not be effective until the completion of this rulemaking."}],"exceptions_text":["except that any judicial challenge that affects such guidelines should not affect drug-testing programs or plans subject to this paragraph","provided that:\n“(a)\n General Rule","provided that:\nPursuant to the provisions of section 4 of Executive Order 11491 [set out as a note under this section], I hereby designate the Director of the Bureau of the Budget [now the Office of Management and Budget] as a member of the Federal Labor Relations Council"],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:12107>EO:12564","names_target":false,"notes":"Machine lead only; no legal ending or revival asserted. Effective date depends on agency, publication or an unstated event. Indirect parent membership is an unconfirmed lead.","provision_label":"","reaches_target_via":"EO:11491 as amended","savings_phrases":["L. 115–271, title VIII, § 8105, Oct. 24, 2018, 132 Stat. 4105, provided that:\n“(a)\n Mandatory Guidelines for Federal Workplace Drug Testing Programs.—\n“(1)\n In general.—\nNot later than 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act [Oct. 24, 2018], the Secretary of Health and Human Services shall—\n“(A)\n determine whether a revision of the Mandatory Guidelines for Federal Workplace Drug Testing Programs to expand the opiate category on the list of authorized substance testing to include fentanyl is justified, based on the reliability and cost-effectiveness of available testing; and\n“(B)\n consider whether to include with the determination under subparagraph (A) a separate determination on whether a revision of the Mandatory Guidelines for Federal Workplace Drug Testing Programs to expand the list of substances authorized for testing to include any other drugs or other substances listed in schedule I and II of section 202 of the Controlled Substances Act (21 U.S.C. 812) is justified based on the criteria described in subparagraph (A).\n“(2)\n Revision of guidelines.—\nIf an expansion of the substance list is determined to be justified under paragraph (1), the Secretary of Health and Human Services shall—\n“(A)\n notify the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives of the determination; and\n“(B)\n publish in the Federal Register, not later than 18 months after the date of the determination under that paragraph, a final notice of the revision of the Mandatory Guidelines for Federal Workplace Drug Testing Programs to expand the list of substances authorized to be tested to include the substance or substances determined to be justified for inclusion.\n“(3)\n Report.—\nIf an expansion of the substance list is determined not to be justified under paragraph (1), the Secretary of Health and Human Services shall submit to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives a report explaining, in detail, the reasons the expansion of the list of authorized substances is not justified.\n“(b)\n Department of Transportation Drug-testing Panel.—\nIf an expansion is determined to be justified under subsection (a)(1), the Secretary of Transportation shall publish in the Federal Register, not later than 18 months after the date the final notice is published under subsection (a)(2), a final rule revising part 40 of title 49, Code of Federal Regulations, to include such substances in the Department of Transportation’s drug-testing panel, consistent with the Mandatory Guidelines for Federal Workplace Drug Testing Programs as revised by the Secretary of Health and Human Services under subsection (a).\n“(c)\n Savings Provision.—\nNothing in this section may be construed as—\n“(1)\n delaying the publication of the notices described in sections 8106 [enacting provisions set out as a note under section 31306 of Title 49, Transportation] and 8107 [enacting provisions set out as a note below] of this Act until the Secretary of Health and Human Services makes a determination or publishes a notice under this section; or\n“(2)\n limiting or otherwise affecting any authority of the Secretary of Health and Human Services or the Secretary of Transportation to expand the list of authorized substance testing to include an additional substance.”\nMandatory Guidelines for Federal Workplace Drug Testing Programs Using Oral Fluid\nPub.","L. 115–271, title VIII, § 8108(a), (b), Oct. 24, 2018, 132 Stat. 4107, provided that:\n“(a)\n Deadline.—\nNot later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act [Oct. 24, 2018], the Secretary of Health and Human Services shall—\n“(1)\n ensure that each certified laboratory that requests approval for the use of completely paperless electronic Federal Drug Testing Custody and Control Forms from the National Laboratory Certification Program’s Electronic Custody and Control Form systems receives approval for those completely paperless electronic forms instead of forms that include any combination of electronic traditional handwritten signatures executed on paper forms; and\n“(2)\n establish a deadline for a certified laboratory to request approval under paragraph (1).\n“(b)\n Savings Clause.—\nNothing in this section [enacting this note and provisions set out as a note under section 322 of Title 49, Transportation] may be construed as limiting or otherwise affecting any authority of the Secretary of Health and Human Services to grant approval to a certified laboratory for use of completely paperless electronic Federal Drug Testing Custody and Control Forms, including to grant approval outside of the process under subsection (a).”\nContinuation of Random Drug Testing Program for Certain Department of Defense Employees\nPub.","Savings Provision."],"scope":"partial","signing_date":"1986-09-15","target_id":"EO:12107","verb":"terminate"}

- **ACT:EO:12107>EO:13467**; S023de79d8eb490afcb428b20; {"actor_id":"EO:13467","char_end":17853,"char_start":17312,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"unknown","effective_date":null,"effective_wording":[{"char_end":1951,"char_start":1347,"text":"Executive branch policies and procedures relating to \nsuitability, contractor employee fitness, eligibility to hold a sensitive position, \naccess to federally controlled facilities and information systems, and eligi-\nbility for access to classified information shall be aligned using consistent \nstandards to the extent possible, provide for reciprocal recognition, and \nshall ensure cost-effective, timely,and efficient protection of the national \ninterest, while providing fair treatment to those upon whom the Federal \nGovernment relies to conduct our Nation’s business and protect national \nsecurity."},{"char_end":8369,"char_start":7558,"text":"(b) The aligned system shall employ updated and consistent standards and \nmethods, enable innovations with enterprise information technology capabili-\nties and end-to-end automation to the extent practicable, and ensure that \nrelevant information maintained by agencies can be accessed and shared \nVerDate Aug<31>2005 18:32 Jul 01, 2008 Jkt 214001 PO 00000 Frm 00004 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\02JYE0.SGM 02JYE0hsrobinson on PROD1PC76 with PROPOSALS2\n=== PDF page 3 of 6 ===\n38105 Federal Register / Vol. 73, No. 128 / Wednesday, July 2, 2008 / Presidential Documents \nrapidly across the executive branch, while protecting national security, pro-\ntecting privacy-related information, ensuring resulting decisions are in the \nnational interest, and providing the Federal Government with an effective \nworkforce."},{"char_end":11953,"char_start":11412,"text":"(e) The Chair may, to ensure the effective implementation of the policy \nset forth in section 1.1 of this order and to the extent consistent with \nlaw, assign, in whole or in part, to the head of any agency (solely or \njointly) any function within the Council ’s responsibility relating to alignment \nand improvement of investigations and determinations of suitability, con-\ntractor employee fitness, eligibility for logical and physical access, eligibility \nfor access to classified information, or eligibility to hold a sensitive position."},{"char_end":12890,"char_start":12501,"text":"As the Suitability Executive Agent, the Director \nof the Office of investiga-\ntions and adjudications relating to determinations of suitability and eligibility \nfor logical and physical access."},{"char_end":15137,"char_start":12980,"text":"The Security Executive \n(vi) shall ensure reciprocal recognition of eligibility for access to classified \ninformation among the agencies, including acting as the final authority \nto arbitrate and resolve disputes among subject to the \nSecurity Executive Agent ’s oversight and with such terms and conditions \n(including approval by the Security Executive Agent) as the Security Execu-\ntive Agent determines Government’s tools, systems, and processes for conducting these \nbackground investigations and managing sensitive investigative information \nshould keep pace with technological advancements, regularly integrating \ncurrent best practices to better anticipate, detect, and counter malicious \nactivities, and threats posed by external or internal actors who may seek \nto do harm to the Government’s personnel, property, and information."},{"char_end":13478,"char_start":12783,"text":"To help fulfill these responsibilities, there shall be a primary executive \nbranch investigative sustained \nby an enhanced risk-management approach that facilitates early detection \nof issues by an informed, aware, and responsible Federal workforce; results \nin quality decisions enabled by improved vetting capabilities; and advances \nGovernment-wide capabilities through enterprise approaches. \n‘‘(d) The appointment or retention of each covered individual shall be \nsubject to an investigation."},{"char_end":23242,"char_start":19592,"text":"It relies on re-\nsearch to generate data-driven decisions and uses outcome-based measure-\nments to adjust policy and operations. \n‘‘(f) 1.3(l) are added to Executive Order 13467 \nto read as follows: \n‘‘(k) ‘Fitness’ means the level of character and conduct determined nec-\nessary for an individual to perform work for or on behalf of a Federal \nagency as an employee in the excepted service (other than a position \nsubject to suitability), or as a ‘contractor employee’ or a ‘nonappropriated \nfund employee’ as those terms are defined in Executive Order 13488 \nof January 16, 2009, as amended. \n‘‘(l) ‘Investigation’ means the collection and analysis of pertinent facts \nand data to support a determination of whether a covered individual \nis, and continues to be: \n‘‘(i) eligible for access to classified information; \n‘‘(ii) eligible to hold a sensitive position; \n‘‘(iii) suitable or fit for Federal employment; \n‘‘(iv) fit to perform work for or on behalf of the Federal Government \nas a contractor or nonappropriated fund employee; or \n‘‘(v) authorized to be issued a Federal credential.’’ \n(k) established within the Office \nof Personnel Management under section 1103(a)(3) of title 5, United States \nCode, or a successor entity, with responsibility for conducting effective, \nefficient, and secure personnel background investigations pursuant to law, \nrule, regulation, or Executive Order.’’ \n(l) Redesignated section 1.3(o) of Executive Order 13467 is revised to \nread as follows: \n‘‘(o) ‘Sensitive Position’ means any position within or in support of a \ndepartment or agency, the occupant of which could bring about, by virtue \nof the nature of the position, a material adverse protecting civil rights and civil liberties, ensuring resulting deci-\nsions are in the national interest and in accordance with due process \nrequirements, and providing the Federal Government with The Director of the Federal Emergency Management Agency is authorized to redelegate, in accord with the provisions of Section 1 (b) of Reorganization Plan No. 1 of 1958 (50 U.S.C. App. 2271 note), any of the functions delegated by Sections 4-101, 4-102, and 4-103 of this Order.\n\n4-105. The functions vested in the Administrator of the Federal Civil Defense Administration by Section 43 of the Act of August 10, 1956 (70A Stat. 636) were transferred to the President by Reorganization Plan No. 1 of 1958, as amended (50 U.S.C. App. 2271 note), were subsequently revested in the Director of the Office of Civil and Defense Mobilization by Section 512 of Public Law 86-500 (50 U.S.C. App. 2285) [the office was changed to Office of Emergency Planning by Public Law 87-296 (75 Stat. 630) and then to the Office of Emergency Preparedness by Section 402 of Public Law 90-608 (82 Stat. 1194)], were again transferred to the President by Section 1 of Reorganization Plan No. I of 1973 (50 U.S.C. App. 2271 note), and they are hereby delegated to the Director of the Federal Emergency Management Agency.\n\n4-106. The functions vested in the Director of the Office of Emergency Preparedness by Section 16 of the Act of September 23, 1950, as amended (20 U.S.C. 646), and by Section 7 of the Act of September 30, 1950, as amended (20 U.S.C. 241-1), were transferred to the President by Section 1 of Reorganization Plan No. 1 of 1973 (50 U.S.C. App. 2271 note), and they are hereby delegated to the Director of the Federal Emergency Management Agency.\n\n4-107. That function vested in the Director of the Office of Emergency Preparedness by Section 762 (a) of the Higher Education Act of 1965, as added by Section 161(a) of the Education Amendments of 1972, and as further amended (20 U.S.G. 1132d-1(a)), to the extent transferred to the President by Reorganization Plan No. 1 of 1973 (50 U.S.C. App. 2271 note), is hereby delegated to the Director of the Federal Emergency Management Agency.\n\n4-2. Delegation of Functions Vested in the President.\n\n4-201. Chapter 58 note), are hereby delegated to the Director of the Federal Emergency Management Agency.\n\n4-202. The functions (related to grants for damages resulting from hurricane and tropical storm Agnes) vested in the President by Section 4 of Public Law 92-385 (86 Stat. 556) are hereby delegated to the Director of the Federal Emergency Management Agency.\n\n4-203. The functions vested in the President by the Disaster Relief Act of 1974 (88 Stat. 143; 42 U.S.C. 5121 et seq.), except those functions vested in the President by Sections 301 (relating to the declaration of emergencies and major disasters), 401 (relating to the repair, reconstruction, restoration, or replacement of Federal facilities), and 409 (relating to food coupons and surplus commodities), are hereby delegated to the Director of the Federal Emergency Management Agency.\n\n4-204. chronology does not decide legal effect.","provision_text":"(1)\n Nothing in subsection (a) shall limit or otherwise affect the availability of funds for drug testing by—\n“(A)\n the Department of Transportation;\n“(B)\n Department of Energy, for employees specifically involved in the handling of nuclear weapons or nuclear materials;\n“(C)\n any agency with an agency-wide drug-testing program in existence as of September 15, 1986; or\n“(D)\n any component of an agency if such component had a drug-testing program in existence as of September 15, 1986.\n“(2)\n The Departments of Transportation and Energy and any agency or component thereof with a drug-testing program in existence as of September 15, 1986—\n“(A)\n shall be brought into full compliance with Executive Order Numbered 12564 [set out as a note below] no later than the end of the 6-month period beginning on the date of the enactment of this Act [July 11, 1987]; and\n“(B)\n shall take such actions as may be necessary to ensure that their respective drug-testing programs or plans are brought into full compliance with the mandatory guidelines published under subsection (a)(1)(A)(ii) no later than 90 days after such mandatory guidelines take effect, except that any judicial challenge that affects such guidelines should not affect drug-testing programs or plans subject to this paragraph.\n“(c)\n In the case of an agency (or component thereof) other than an agency as defined by subsection (a)(2) or an agency (or component thereof) covered by subsection (b), none of the funds appropriated or made available by this Act, or any other Act, with respect to any fiscal year, shall be available to administer or implement any drug testing pursuant to Executive Order Numbered 12564 [set out as a note below], or any subsequent order, unless and until—\n“(1)\n the Secretary of Health and Human Services provides written certification with respect to that agency (or component) in accordance with clauses (i) and (iii) of subsection (a)(1)(A);\n“(2)\n the Secretary of Health and Human Services has submitted a written, detailed analysis with respect to that agency (or component) in accordance with subsection (a)(1)(B); and\n“(3)\n the Director of the Office of Management and Budget has submitted a written, detailed analysis with respect to that agency (or component) in accordance with subsection (a)(1)(C).\n“(d)\n Any Federal employee who is the subject of a drug test under any program or plan shall, upon written request, have access to—\n“(1)\n any records relating to such employee’s drug test; and\n“(2)\n any records relating to the results of any relevant certification, review, or revocation-of-certification proceedings, as referred to in subsection (a)(1)(A)(ii)(III).\n“(e)\n The results of a drug test of a Federal employee may not be disclosed without the prior written consent of such employee, unless the disclosure would be—\n“(1)\n to the employee’s medical review official (as defined in the scientific and technical guidelines referred to in subsection (a)(1)(A)(ii));\n“(2)\n to the administrator of any Employee Assistance Program in which the employee is receiving counseling or treatment or is otherwise participating;\n“(3)\n to any supervisory or management official within the employee’s agency having authority to take the adverse personnel action against such employee; or\n“(4)\n pursuant to the order of a court of competent jurisdiction where required by the United States Government to defend against any challenge against any adverse personnel action.\n“(f)\n [Terminated, effective May 15, 2000, see section 3003 of Pub. L. 104–66, as amended, set out as a note under section 1113 of Title 31, Money and Finance, and page 151 of House Document No. 103–7.]\n“(g)\n For purposes of this section, the terms ‘agency’ and ‘Employee Assistance Program’ each has the meaning given such term under section 7(b) of Executive Order Numbered 12564 [set out as a note below], as in effect on September 15, 1986.”\n[For abolition of United States Information Agency (other than Broadcasting Board of Governors and International Broadcasting Bureau), transfer of functions, and treatment of references thereto, see sections 6531, 6532, and 6551 of Title 22, Foreign Relations and Intercourse.]\nLimitation on Gratuities at Naval Shipbuilding Ceremonies\nPub. L. 99–145, title XIV, § 1461, Nov. 8, 1985, 99 Stat. 765, provided that:\n“(a)\n General Rule.—\nA Federal officer, employee, or Member of Congress may not accept, directly or indirectly, any tangible thing of value as a gift or memento in connection with a ceremony to mark the completion of a naval shipbuilding milestone.\n“(b)\n Exclusion.—\nSubsection (a) does not apply to a gift or memento that has a value of less than $100.\n“(c)\n Definitions.—\nFor purposes of this section, the terms ‘officer’, ‘employee’, and ‘Member of Congress’ have the meanings given those terms in sections 2104, 2105, and 2106, respectively, of title 5, United States Code.”\nExecutive Documents\nEmergency Preparedness Functions\nFor assignment of certain emergency preparedness functions to the Director of the Office of Personnel Management, see Parts 1, 2, and 22 of Ex. Ord. No. 12656, Nov. 18, 1988, 53 F.R. 47491, set out as a note under section 5195 of Title 42, The Public Health and Welfare.\nDesignation of Director of the Bureau of the Budget as Member of Federal Labor Relations Council\nPresidential Order of December 8, 1969, provided that:\nPursuant to the provisions of section 4 of Executive Order 11491 [set out as a note under this section], I hereby designate the Director of the Bureau of the Budget [now the Office of Management and Budget] as a member of the Federal Labor Relations Council. This order of designation shall be published in the Federal Register.\nRichard Nixon.\nExecutive Order No. 9845\nEx. Ord. No. 9845, Apr. 28, 1947, 12 F.R. 2799, which permitted Bureau of Reclamation employees to accept appointments as constables or deputy sheriffs under state or territorial laws, was revoked by Ex. Ord. No. 11408, Apr. 25, 1968, 33 F.R. 6459.\nEx. Ord. No. 12564. Drug-Free Federal Workplace\nEx. Ord. No. 12564, Sept. 15, 1986, 51 F.R. 32889, provided:\nI, RONALD REAGAN, President of the United States of America, find that:\nDrug use is having serious adverse effects upon a significant proportion of the national work force and results in billions of dollars of lost productivity each year;\nThe Federal government, as an employer, is concerned with the well-being of its employees, the successful accomplishment of agency missions, and the need to maintain employee productivity;\nThe Federal government, as the largest employer in the Nation, can and should show the way towards achieving drug-free workplaces through a program designed to offer drug users a helping hand and, at the same time, demonstrating to drug users and potential drug users that drugs will not be tolerated in the Federal workplace;\nThe profits from illegal drugs provide the single greatest source of income for organized crime, fuel violent street crime, and otherwise contribute to the breakdown of our society;\nThe use of illegal drugs, on or off duty, by Federal employees is inconsistent not only with the law-abiding behavior expected of all citizens, but also with the special trust placed in such employees as servants of the public;\nFederal employees who use illegal drugs, on or off duty, tend to be less productive, less reliable, and prone to greater absenteeism than their fellow employees who do not use illegal drugs;\nThe use of illegal drugs, on or off duty, by Federal employees impairs the efficiency of Federal departments and agencies, undermines public confidence in them, and makes it more difficult for other employees who do not use illegal drugs to perform their jobs effectively. The use of illegal drugs, on or off duty, by Federal employees also can pose a serious health and safety threat to members of the public and to other Federal employees;\nThe use of illegal drugs, on or off duty, by Federal employees in certain positions evidences less than the complete reliability, stability, and good judgment that is consistent with access to sensitive information and creates the possibility of coercion, influence, and irresponsible action under pressure that may pose a serious risk to national security, the public safety, and the effective enforcement of the law; and\nFederal employees who use illegal drugs must themselves be primarily responsible for changing their behavior and, if necessary, begin the process of rehabilitating themselves.\nBy the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and laws of the United States of America, including section 3301(2) of Title 5 of the United States Code, section 7301 of Title 5 of the United States Code, section 290ee–1 of Title 42 of the United States Code, deeming such action in the best interests of national security, public health and safety, law enforcement and the efficiency of the Federal service, and in order to establish standards and procedures to ensure fairness in achieving a drug-free Federal workplace and to protect the privacy of Federal employees, it is hereby ordered as follows:","sections_touched":["section 3003","section 1113","section 7(b)","sections 6531","sections 2104","Parts 1","section 5195","section 4","section 3301(2)","section 7301","section 290"],"signing_date":"1986-09-15","source":{"acceptable_as_original":false,"filing_date":null,"grade":"held_text_lead","instrument_id":"EO:12564","page_or_item":"5 U.S.C. 7301","requires_page_check":false,"sha256":"ed3ba438ffd040def329beea813ce0a7382027b9103dd5a39c0d4b489110239e","signing_date":"1986-09-15","text_path":"jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t5-s7301.txt","text_sha256":"ed3ba438ffd040def329beea813ce0a7382027b9103dd5a39c0d4b489110239e","url":"https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-prelim-title5-section7301&num=0&edition=prelim"},"verb":"terminate"},{"actor_id":"EO:13467","char_end":17853,"char_start":17312,"confidence":"medium","how_named":"parent_as_amended","id":"CHAIN:EO:12107#9","notes":"Change wording lead; - **ACT:EO:12591>EO:12618**; S837b75f14883c0e0a13121a4; {"actor_id":"EO:12618","char_end":2182,"char_start":594,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"unknown","effective_date":null,"effective_wording":[{"char_end":2182,"char_start":594,"text":"Title 3— Executive Order 12618 of December 22, 1987\nUniform Treatment of Federally Funded InventionsThe President\nBy the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and laws of the \nUnited States of America, and having concluded that the ability of the United \nStates to achieve the statutorily prescribed policy (35 U.S.C. 200) of using the \npatent system to promote the utilization of inventions arising from federally \nsupported research or development requires that Federal agencies follow \nuniform policies in administering patents and licenses conceived or first \nreduced to practice during the course of federally funded research, Executive \nOrder No. 12591 of April 10,1987, is amended by redesignating Sections 1(b)(5) \nand (6) as 1(b)(6) and (7), respectively, and by adding a new Section 1(b)(5) as\n‘(5) administer all patents and licenses to inventions made with federal \nassistance, which are owned by the non-profit contractor or grantee, in \naccordance with Section 202(c)(7) of Title 35 of the United States Code as \namended by Public Law 98-620, without regard to limitations on licensing \nfound in that section prior to amendment or in Institutional Patent Agreements \nnow in effect that were entered into before that law was enacted on Novem­\nber 8,1984, unless, in the case of an invention that has not been marketed, the \nfunding agency determines, based on information in its files, that the contrac­\ntor or grantee has not taken adequate steps to market the inventions, in \naccordance with applicable law or an Institutional Patent Agreement;”.\nfollows:"}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:12591>EO:12618","names_target":true,"notes":"Machine lead only; no legal ending or revival asserted.
